subject: Post-demo: delegated notice, log SLA & DPA clarifications
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Morris <dana@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: delegated notice, log SLA & DPA clarifications

Hi Dana —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and three ask areas so we can move the DPA/contract conversation forward: 

1) Who is the data controller in your expected deployment? You mentioned Acme Health would remain controller for patient records, but we'd like confirmation for the narrow scope of inference logs and telemetry.

2) Breach notification timing — you flagged a 48-hour requirement during the call. We typically operate on a 72-hour notification SLA for hosted customers; please confirm whether 48 hours is a hard requirement for your procurement/legal team.

3) Logs & residency — please confirm desired retention for request/trace logs and whether logs must be stored within EU/US only. Our default hosted retention is 90 days; we can extend retention and offer region pinning for enterprise contracts.

Attached is a short DPA summary and the post-demo slide with the proposed dataflow. Can you also send your privacy questionnaire (if you have one) so we can map answers back to the DPA?

Proposed next steps: 
- We’ll loop Legal (Laura) for the formal DPA language and subprocessor details.
- I’ll share our subprocessor register and SOC2 report once we confirm the residency/retention asks.
- If helpful, suggest a 30-minute legal sync early next week to finalize the notify SLA and retention scope.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(j) 415-555-0198
redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-dpa-summary.pdf (summary), demo-dataflow-slide.pdf (slide)

From: Dana Morris <dana@acmehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health Security <security@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 16:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Post-demo: delegated notice, log SLA & DPA clarifications

Hi Jordan,

Appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Controller: Acme Health will be the controller for all patient PHI. For telemetry and inference request logs that contain pseudonymous identifiers, we still expect Acme to be controller; Redwood will act as processor.

- Breach notify: Our legal team requires a 48-hour initial notification window for incidents that materially affect PHI. We understand this is tighter than your standard; please indicate whether Redwood can commit contractually or if we should treat this as a negotiation point.

- Subprocessors: We need the current subprocessor register and a commitment to provide at least 30 days' notice before onboarding new subprocessors that will handle Acme data.

- Logs & retention: For regulated services, Acme requires 24 months of request/trace log retention for display/audit; residency must be configurable to keep logs within US-based regions. EU residency is not required for us at this time but we may revisit for future accounts.

Attached is our privacy questionnaire (filled in by security) — items 8–12 map to the breach workflow and subprocessor rules.

Happy to do a 30-minute legal sync Tue/Wed next week — preferred times: Tue 10–11am PT or Wed 1–3pm PT.

Thanks,
Dana Morris
Head of IT Security, Acme Health
security@acmehealth.com

Attachments: acme-privacy-questionnaire.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: delegated notice, log SLA & DPA clarifications

Hi Dana —

Thanks for the questionnaire and the clear requirements. Below are answers and proposed contract language/next steps. I’ve attached our current subprocessor register and the most recent SOC2 report for your review.

1) Controller / Processor
- Confirmation: Acme Health will be the Controller; Redwood Inference will act as Processor for data processing carried out on behalf of Acme per the standard DPA. If there are any services where Redwood independently determines processing purposes (e.g., industry-wide analytics aggregated and anonymized), we will call that out in the DPA; otherwise Acme is Controller.

Proposed DPA snippet: "Customer is Controller; Redwood Inference is Processor with authority to engage subprocessors as set out in the Subprocessor Register. Any analytics performed by Redwood on aggregated, non-identifiable data will be explicitly scoped and excluded from Controller data obligations."

2) Breach notification timing
- Standard: Redwood’s production practice is to provide initial incident notification within 72 hours of detection for incidents affecting customer data.
- Enterprise option: We can commit contractually to an initial notification within 48 hours for PHI-impacting incidents as an enterprise SLA item; this requires inclusion in the SOW/Order Form and is subject to standard carve-outs (e.g., ongoing investigation, law enforcement).

Proposed DPA snippet: "Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide Customer with an initial notification of security incidents affecting Customer data within 48 hours of detection for incidents materially affecting PHI where Customer has purchased the 48-hour notification SLA in the Order Form."

3) Subprocessors and notice
- We will provide the current Subprocessor Register (attached). For hosted customers, Redwood provides notice of new subprocessors via email and an online register. We can commit to at least 30 days' prior notice for new subprocessors that will have access to Customer data and offer Customer the right to object in writing within that period under defined grounds.

Proposed DPA snippet: "Redwood will provide Customer at least thirty (30) days' prior notice via email of any new subprocessor engaged to process Customer data and will publish the Subprocessor Register online. Customer may object to the appointment of a new subprocessor on reasonable grounds related to data protection; the parties will use good faith efforts to resolve any objection."

4) Logs, retention & residency
- Default: Hosted customers: request/trace logs retained 90 days by default.
- Enterprise amendment: We can offer an account-scoped retention extension to 24 months as a paid contract add-on; this will be reflected in the Order Form.
- Residency: For hosted customers we support region selection (US or EU) for data storage. For strict residency guarantees (including log pinning in a specified region for longer retention), we recommend Redwood Private (VPC) or an enterprise clause in the Order Form.

Proposed DPA snippet: "Redwood will retain request/trace logs per the retention period selected in Customer's Order Form. Redwood offers default retention of 90 days; Customer may purchase extended retention (up to 24 months) as set forth in the Order Form. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to store logs in the geographic region specified in the Order Form for hosted customers; for contractual residency guarantees, the parties will use the Private deployment clause."

5) Evidence & attachments
- Attached: redwood-subprocessor-register.csv, redwood-soc2-2027.pdf
- We can provide redacted audit evidence on request under an NDA for procurement review.

6) Next steps & scheduling
- If Acme needs the 48-hour notification as a hard requirement, include the 48-hour SLA in the draft Order Form and we will route for internal approvals.
- I recommend a 30-minute sync to confirm the Order Form language. Proposed times: Tue 16 May 2028 10:30am PT or Tue 16 May 2028 11:30am PT (Jordan / Dana — please confirm).

Happy to make the language tighter if your legal team has specific redlines.

Best regards,

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
